results.attack: Attacker B sends 13 requests with victim A's bucket, transaction and report ids across Buckets, Transactions and Insights
results.expected: every request refused (404/403/4xx), A's data unchanged
results.note: GET /api/buckets/<A-id> → 404; PATCH /api/buckets/<A-id> → 404; DELETE /api/buckets/<A-id> → 404; POST /api/buckets/<A-id>/archive → 404; POST /api/buckets/<A-id>/check-spend → 404; POST /api/buckets/transfers → 400; GET /api/transactions/<A-id> → 404; PATCH /api/transactions/<A-id> → 404; DELETE /api/transactions/<A-id> → 404; GET /api/transactions/<A-id>/receipt → 404; POST /api/transactions → 400; GET /api/insights/reports/<A-id>/download → 404; DELETE /api/insights/reports/<A-id> → 404

results.attack: 15 forged or misplaced tokens claiming to be victim A as admin
results.note: HS256 signed with guessed key "secret" → 401; HS256 signed with guessed key "changeme" → 401; HS256 signed with guessed key "password" → 401; HS256 signed with guessed key "jwt-secret" → 401; HS256 signed with guessed key "pb-jwt-secret" → 401; HS256 signed with guessed key "personal-budget-buckets" → 401; HS256 signed with guessed key "" → 401; alg "HS512" → 401; alg "none", empty signature → 401; alg "None" (case trick) → 401; jku header pointing to attacker keys → 401; kid path traversal (../../dev/null, empty key) → 401; B's real signature with A's id swapped in → 401; B's real token with signature removed → 401; token in a query string instead of the header → 401

results.attack: 12 NoSQL/SQL-style, operator, type-confusion, path and prototype-pollution payloads
results.expected: all rejected by validation (400/401/404/422); no 500; pollution does not give admin
results.note: login with {"$ne": null} as e-mail and password → 400; login with e-mail "a@b.c' OR 1=1 --" → 401; bucket with monthlyLimit as an object → 400; bucket with monthlyLimit as an array → 400; bucket with monthlyLimit 1e309 (Infinity) → 400; bucket with monthlyLimit -500 → 400; expense with amount "100; DROP TABLE" → 400; expense with amount 0.000001 → 400; expense dated 9999-12-31 → 400; bucket id "../../USER#<A>" in the path → 404; month query "2026-11' OR '1'='1" → 400; __proto__ pollution in body → 400; B on admin endpoint afterwards → 403

results.attack: B creates a bucket with pk/sk/userId/id/status of victim A in the body; A tries to move a transaction to B by PATCHing userId/pk
results.expected: extra fields ignored or refused: nothing planted in A's account, the transaction stays A's
results.actual: bucket refused 400; planted in A: no; PATCH → 400, still A's: yes

results.attack: 10 expenses of 30 sent at the same moment to a bucket with a hard limit of 100
results.expected: at most 3 accepted (90), total spent never above 100

results.attack: 20 wrong passwords sent in parallel to one account (lockout is after 5)
results.expected: at most 5 guesses checked, then locked (429); the right password is then refused while locked
results.actual: 5 guesses checked (401), 5 got 429; right password afterwards → 429

results.attack: Compare login answers and timing for a real and a made-up e-mail; register an e-mail that exists
results.expected: login: same status, message and similar timing; register: reveals the e-mail exists (accepted risk, see note)
results.actual: login same answer: yes (401); avg time 62 ms vs 65 ms; register existing → 409 EMAIL_TAKEN
results.note: Register says EMAIL_TAKEN, so sign-up can confirm an account exists. Most sites accept this for usability; the mitigations are the API rate limit and the CloudWatch FailedLogins alarm.

results.attack: Malformed JSON, unknown and traversal paths, TRACE, null byte
results.expected: short JSON errors with no stack trace, file path or library name; no X-Powered-By; security headers present
results.actual: 0 responses leaked internals; X-Powered-By absent; nosniff + HSTS present; statuses 400, 400, 404, refused by client, 400

results.attack: Bucket named with an script payload, then check how the frontend would show it
results.expected: API stores it as plain text or rejects it; frontend writes names with textContent/escaping; CSP present
results.actual: API → 201 (stored as text: true); CSP meta tag: yes; unescaped HTML sinks in the frontend scripts: 0
results.note: unescaped sinks = lines that assign innerHTML without an escape helper

results.attack: 60 requests at once from one user (stage limit 10/s, burst 20; Lambda reserved concurrency)
results.expected: excess requests refused with 429 or 503, service still answers afterwards

results.attack: Unsigned (anonymous) list and upload on the receipts, reports and audit-log buckets
results.expected: 403 for every request; where the emulator cannot enforce it, the bucket settings that AWS enforces must block all public access
results.actual: anonymous: pb-receipts-244694: list 200, put 200; pb-reports-244694: list 200, put 200; pb-audit-logs-244694: list 200, put not tried (write-once bucket) → Floci does not enforce S3 signatures. Settings: pb-receipts-244694: Block Public Access True/True/True/True, public policy none, public ACL grants none; pb-reports-244694: Block Public Access True/True/True/True, public policy none, public ACL grants none; pb-audit-logs-244694: Block Public Access True/True/True/True, public policy False, public ACL grants none
results.note: PASS by configuration, not by an enforced 403: Floci treats every S3 call as the account owner. On AWS, Block Public Access (all 4 settings) makes unsigned requests fail with 403.
